claims.quote: The most common cause of DS is haploinsufficiency of the SCN1A gene
which encodes the voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.1.
we report the generation and characterization of a Scn1a halploinsufficiency rat model of DS by disrupting the Scn1a allele.

claims.object_text: reduced SCN1A expression in cerebral cortex, hippocampus and thalamus
claims.quote: Scn1a+/- rats show reduced Scn1a expression in the cerebral cortex, hippocampus and thalamus.

claims.object_text: premature death of homozygous null rats

claims.quote: Heterozygous animals are highly susceptible to heat-induced seizures, the clinical hallmark of DS, but are otherwise normal in survival, growth, and behavior without seizure induction.

claims.object_text: activation of distinct sets of neurons in hippocampus and hypothalamus during hyperthermia-induced seizures
claims.quote: Hyperthermia-induced seizures activate distinct sets of neurons in the hippocampus and hypothalamus in Scn1a+/- rats.

claims.object_text: ictal EEG with high amplitude bursts and increased delta and theta power
claims.quote: Electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings in Scn1a+/- rats reveal characteristic ictal EEG with high amplitude bursts with significantly increased delta and theta power.

claims.object_text: spontaneous non-convulsive and convulsive seizures following initial hyperthermia-induced seizures
claims.quote: After the initial hyperthermia-induced seizures, non-convulsive, and convulsive seizures occur spontaneously in Scn1a+/- rats.
